ruleName: Ball moved when grounding the club
title: Penalty for moving the ball when grounding the club
question: You accidentally move your ball on the fairway by grounding your club behind it. What must you do according to the rules?

choices.text: No penalty, play the ball from where it moved to.
Replace the ball and add 1 penalty stroke.
Add two penalty strokes and carry on.
Replace the ball with no penalty.

explanation: If you move your ball by grounding your club behind it on the fairway, the correct action is to replace the ball and add one penalty stroke.

juniorVersion.title: What happens if you move your ball with your club?
juniorVersion.question: You put your club down behind your ball on the fairway and the ball rolls away by accident. What should you do?

choices.text: No penalty. Hit your ball from its new place.
Put your ball back where it was and add 1 penalty shot.
Add two penalty shots and keep playing.
Put your ball back and no penalty.

juniorVersion.explanation: If you make your ball move by putting your club on the ground behind it, you must put your ball back and add one penalty shot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short grass you aim for between the tee and the green.
Letting your club touch the ground before you swing.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show the children how to carefully put their club behind the ball without moving it. Practise where to rest the club gently.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they can hit the ball from where it moved to.
Some may forget to add the penalty stroke.
